45	 * Name: nxsem_wait_slow
46	 *
47	 * Description:
48	 *   This function attempts to lock the semaphore referenced by 'sem' in
49	 *   slow mode.
50	 *
51	 *   This is an internal OS interface.  It is functionally equivalent to
52	 *   sem_wait except that:
53	 *
54	 *   - It is not a cancellation point, and
55	 *   - It does not modify the errno value.
56	 *
57	 * Input Parameters:
58	 *   sem - Semaphore descriptor.
59	 *
60	 * Returned Value:
61	 *   This is an internal OS interface and should not be used by applications.
62	 *   It follows the NuttX internal error return policy:  Zero (OK) is
63	 *   returned on success.  A negated errno value is returned on failure.
64	 *   Possible returned errors:
65	 *
66	 *   - EINVAL:  Invalid attempt to get the semaphore
67	 *   - EINTR:   The wait was interrupted by the receipt of a signal.
68	 *
69	 ****************************************************************************/
70	
71	int nxsem_wait_slow(FAR sem_t *sem)
72	{
73	  FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
74	  irqstate_t flags;
75	  int ret = OK;
76	  bool unlocked;
77	  int32_t mholder;
78	  FAR struct tcb_s *htcb = NULL;
79	  bool mutex = NXSEM_IS_MUTEX(sem);
80	
81	  /* The following operations must be performed with interrupts
82	   * disabled because nxsem_post() may be called from an interrupt
83	   * handler.
84	   */
85	
86	  flags = enter_critical_section();
87	
88	  /* Make sure we were supplied with a valid semaphore. */
89	
90	  /* Check if the lock is available */
91	
92	  if (mutex)
93	    {
94	      /* We lock the mutex for us by setting the blocks bit,
95	       * this is all that is needed if we block
96	       */
97	
98	      mholder = atomic_or(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT);
99	
100	      /* Avoid mutex recursion, which is not allowed. */
101	
102	      DEBUGASSERT((mholder & (~NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT)) != nxsched_gettid());
103	
104	      if (NXSEM_MACQUIRED(mholder))
105	        {
106	          /* htcb gets NULL if
107	           * - the only holder did exit (without posting first)
108	           * - the mutex was reset before
109	           * In both cases we simply acquire the mutex, thus recovering
110	           * from these situations.
111	           */
112	
113	          htcb = nxsched_get_tcb(mholder & (~NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT));
114	        }
115	
116	      unlocked = htcb == NULL;
117	      if (!unlocked)
118	        {
119	          nxsem_add_holder_tcb(htcb, sem);
120	          nxsched_put_tcb(htcb);
121	        }
122	    }
123	  else
124	    {
125	      unlocked = atomic_sub(NXSEM_COUNT(sem), 1) > 0;
126	    }
127	
128	  if (unlocked)
129	    {
130	      /* It is, let the task take the semaphore. */
131	
132	#ifdef CONFIG_PRIORITY_PROTECT
133	      ret = nxsem_protect_wait(sem);
134	      if (ret < 0)
135	        {
136	          if (mutex)
137	            {
138	              atomic_set(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), NXSEM_NO_MHOLDER);
139	            }
140	          else
141	            {
142	              atomic_add(NXSEM_COUNT(sem), 1);
143	            }
144	
145	          leave_critical_section(flags);
146	          return ret;
147	        }
148	#endif
149	
150	      /* For mutexes, we only add the holder to the tasks list at the
151	       * time when a task blocks on the mutex, for priority restoration
152	       */
153	
154	      if (mutex)
155	        {
156	          mholder = rtcb->pid;
157	
158	          if (!dq_empty(SEM_WAITLIST(sem)))
159	            {
160	              mholder |= NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT;
161	            }
162	
163	          atomic_set(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), mholder);
164	        }
165	      else
166	        {
167	          nxsem_add_holder(sem);
168	        }
169	    }
170	
171	  /* The semaphore is NOT available, We will have to block the
172	   * current thread of execution.
173	   */
174	
175	  else
176	    {
177	#ifdef CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE
178	      uint8_t prioinherit = sem->flags & SEM_PRIO_MASK;
179	#endif
180	
181	      /* First, verify that the task is not already waiting on a
182	       * semaphore
183	       */
184	
185	      DEBUGASSERT(rtcb->waitobj == NULL);
186	
187	      /* Save the waited on semaphore in the TCB */
188	
189	      rtcb->waitobj = sem;
190	
191	      /* If priority inheritance is enabled, then check the priority of
192	       * the holder of the semaphore.
193	       */
194	
195	#ifdef CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE
196	      if (prioinherit == SEM_PRIO_INHERIT)
197	        {
198	          /* Disable context switching.  The following operations must be
199	           * atomic with regard to the scheduler.
200	           */
201	
202	          sched_lock();
203	
204	          /* Boost the priority of any threads holding a count on the
205	           * semaphore.
206	           */
207	
208	          nxsem_boost_priority(sem);
209	        }
210	#endif
211	
212	      /* Set the errno value to zero (preserving the original errno)
213	       * value).  We reuse the per-thread errno to pass information
214	       * between sem_waitirq() and this functions.
215	       */
216	
217	      rtcb->errcode = OK;
218	
219	      /* Add the TCB to the prioritized semaphore wait queue, after
220	       * checking this is not the idle task - descheduling that
221	       * isn't going to end well.
222	       */
223	
224	      DEBUGASSERT(!is_idle_task(rtcb));
225	
226	      /* Remove the tcb task from the running list. */
227	
228	      nxsched_remove_self(rtcb);
229	
230	      /* Add the task to the specified blocked task list */
231	
232	      rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_WAIT_SEM;
233	      nxsched_add_prioritized(rtcb, SEM_WAITLIST(sem));
234	
235	      /* Now, perform the context switch */
236	
237	      nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
238	
239	      /* When we resume at this point, either (1) the semaphore has been
240	       * assigned to this thread of execution, or (2) the semaphore wait
241	       * has been interrupted by a signal or a timeout.  We can detect
242	       * these latter cases be examining the per-thread errno value.
243	       *
244	       * In the event that the semaphore wait was interrupted by a
245	       * signal or a timeout, certain semaphore clean-up operations have
246	       * already been performed (see sem_waitirq.c).  Specifically:
247	       *
248	       * - nxsem_canceled() was called to restore the priority of all
249	       *   threads that hold a reference to the semaphore,
250	       * - The semaphore count was decremented, and
251	       * - tcb->waitobj was nullifed.
252	       *
253	       * It is necessary to do these things in sem_waitirq.c because a
254	       * long time may elapse between the time that the signal was issued
255	       * and this thread is awakened and this leaves a door open to
256	       * several race conditions.
257	       */
258	
259	      /* Check if an error occurred while we were sleeping.  Expected
260	       * errors include EINTR meaning that we were awakened by a signal
261	       * or ETIMEDOUT meaning that the timer expired for the case of
262	       * sem_timedwait().
263	       *
264	       * If we were not awakened by a signal or a timeout, then
265	       * nxsem_add_holder() was called by logic in sem_wait() fore this
266	       * thread was restarted.
267	       */
268	
269	      ret = rtcb->errcode != OK ? -rtcb->errcode : OK;
270	
271	#ifdef CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE
272	      if (prioinherit != 0)
273	        {
274	          sched_unlock();
275	        }
276	#endif
277	    }
278	
279	  leave_critical_section(flags);
280	
281	  return ret;
282	}

45	void restore_context(FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb, FAR struct tcb_s *wtcb,
46	                     FAR sem_t *sem, int errcode, bool mutex)
47	{
48	  /* This restores the value to what it was before the previous sem_wait.
49	   * This caused the thread to be blocked in the first place.
50	   *
51	   * For mutexes, the holder is updated by the thread itself
52	   * when it exits nxsem_wait
53	   */

56	    {

58	    }
59	  else if (dq_empty(SEM_WAITLIST(sem)))
60	    {
61	      atomic_and(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), ~NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT);
62	    }

65	
66	  wtcb->waitobj = NULL;

69	
70	  wtcb->errcode = (int16_t)errcode;

73	   * perform the context switch if one is needed
74	   */
75

88	 *

90	 *   This function is called when either:
91	 *
92	 *   1. A signal is received by a task that is waiting on a semaphore.
93	 *      According to the POSIX spec, "...the calling thread shall not return
94	 *      from the call to [nxsem_wait] until it either locks the semaphore or
95	 *      the call is interrupted by a signal."
96	 *   2. From logic associated with sem_timedwait().  This function is called
97	 *      when the timeout elapses without receiving the semaphore.
98	 *
99	 *   Note: this function should used within critical_section
100	 *
101	 * Input Parameters:
102	 *   wtcb    - A pointer to the TCB of the task that is waiting on a
103	 *             semphaphore, but has received a signal or timeout instead.
104	 *   errcode - EINTR if the semaphore wait was awakened by a signal;
105	 *             ETIMEDOUT if awakened by a timeout
106	 *

108	 *   None

118	  bool mutex;
119	
120	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV

125	      addrenv_select(wtcb->group->tg_addrenv_own, &oldenv);
126	    }
127	#endif

130	   * and already changed the task's state.
131	   */
132	
133	  DEBUGASSERT(sem != NULL);
134	
135	  mutex = NXSEM_IS_MUTEX(sem);
136	
137	  DEBUGASSERT(mutex || atomic_read(NXSEM_COUNT(sem)) < 0);
138	  DEBUGASSERT(!mutex || NXSEM_MBLOCKING(atomic_read(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem))));
139	
140	  /* Mutex is never interrupted by a signal or canceled */
141	
142	  if (mutex && (errcode == EINTR || errcode == ECANCELED))
143	    {
144	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
145	      if (wtcb->group->tg_addrenv_own)
146	        {
147	          addrenv_restore(oldenv);
148	        }
149	#endif
150	    }
151	  else
152	    {
153	      /* Restore the correct priority of all threads that hold references
154	       * to this semaphore.
155	       */
156	
157	      nxsem_canceled(wtcb, sem);
158	
159	      /* Remove task from waiting list */
160	
161	      dq_rem((FAR dq_entry_t *)wtcb, SEM_WAITLIST(sem));
162	
163	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
164	      if (wtcb->group->tg_addrenv_own)
165	        {
166	          addrenv_restore(oldenv);
167	        }
168	#endif
169	
170	      restore_context(rtcb, wtcb, sem, errcode, mutex);
171	    }

47	 * Name: nxtask_recover
48	 *
49	 * Description:
50	 *   This function is called when a task is deleted via task_delete() or
51	 *   via pthread_cancel.  I checks checks for semaphores, message queue, and
52	 *   watchdog timer resources stranded in bad conditions.
53	 *
54	 * Input Parameters:
55	 *   tcb - The TCB of the terminated task or thread
56	 *
57	 * Returned Value:
58	 *   None.
59	 *
60	 * Assumptions:
61	 *   This function is called from task deletion logic in a safe context.
62	 *
63	 ****************************************************************************/
64	
65	void nxtask_recover(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb)
66	{
67	#if !defined(CONFIG_DISABLE_PTHREAD) && !defined(CONFIG_PTHREAD_MUTEX_UNSAFE)
68	  /* Recover any mutexes still held by the canceled thread */
69	
70	  pthread_mutex_inconsistent(nxsched_get_tls(tcb));
71	#endif
72	
73	  /* The task is being deleted.  Cancel in pending timeout events. */
74	
75	  wd_cancel(&tcb->waitdog);
76	
77	  /* If the thread holds semaphore counts or is waiting for a semaphore
78	   *  count, then release the counts.
79	   */
80	
81	  nxsem_recover(tcb);
82	
83	#if !defined(CONFIG_DISABLE_MQUEUE) || !defined(CONFIG_DISABLE_MQUEUE_SYSV)
84	  /* Handle cases where the thread was waiting for a message queue event */
85	
86	  nxmq_recover(tcb);
87	#endif
88	
89	#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
90	  if ((atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
91	      TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
92	    {
93	      /* Stop current sporadic scheduling */
94	
95	      DEBUGVERIFY(nxsched_stop_sporadic(tcb));
96	    }
97	#endif
98	}

But then... nxsem_wait_irq with EINTR for a non-mutex semaphore DOES remove the task from the waitlist and wake it. Then in `nxsem_wait_slow`, ret = -EINTR. THAT is the "uninterruptible" behavior in this tree: the header-level retry loop.

So SIGTERM/SIGKILL wake the task, it returns -EINTR, and `nxsem_wait_uninterruptible` immediately re-waits. The task is never unblocked permanently. This exactly explains "blocked forever" and "still alive".

function(myvendor_patch_target_by_name target ov_dir)
  if(NOT TARGET ${target})
    return()
  endif()

  if(NOT EXISTS "${ov_dir}")
    return()
  endif()

  file(GLOB _ov_files "${ov_dir}/*.c")
  if(NOT _ov_files)
    return()
  endif()

  set(_ov_names)
  foreach(_f IN LISTS _ov_files)
    get_filename_component(_n "${_f}" NAME)
    list(APPEND _ov_names "${_n}")
  endforeach()

  get_target_property(_srcs ${target} SOURCES)
  if(NOT _srcs)
    return()
  endif()

  set(_kept)
  set(_used)
  foreach(_src IN LISTS _srcs)
    get_filename_component(_n "${_src}" NAME)
    if(_n IN_LIST _ov_names)
      list(APPEND _used "${_n}")
    else()
      list(APPEND _kept "${_src}")
    endif()
  endforeach()

  if(NOT _used)
    message(WARNING "my_vendor: ${ov_dir} .c not in ${target}")
    return()
  endif()

  set_property(TARGET ${target} PROPERTY SOURCES ${_kept})
  foreach(_n IN LISTS _used)
    target_sources(${target} PRIVATE "${ov_dir}/${_n}")
    message(STATUS "my_vendor: ${target} uses board ${_n}")
  endforeach()

  foreach(_n IN LISTS _ov_names)
    if(NOT _n IN_LIST _used)
      message(WARNING "my_vendor: override ${_n} not in ${target}, skipped")
    endif()
  endforeach()
endfunction()
